title: Concentrate errors to cure them: weak-bit symbol herding
idea: Paradox: making errors burstier makes them more correctable. A small Benes permutation network on the data path, configured per row from test/boot fault data, routes all known weak or failing bits of a row into the same Reed-Solomon symbol, so eight scattered weak bits that would overwhelm a symbol code count as a single symbol error.
why: Raises tolerable weak-cell density per row ~4-8x under the same RS code, letting higher-defect (denser, cheaper) arrays ship; cost is a few gate delays and a per-row config index.
note: Permutation network concentrates known weak bits into one RS symbol.

title: Wound-capacitor memory: thin-film bit tape rolled into 3D cylinders
idea: A 1955 engineer's wound paper capacitor applied to memory: fabricate a thin-film memory array on meters of polyimide or steel-foil tape roll-to-roll, then wind it into a cylinder whose bitlines all exit at the end faces, where laser-patterned flame-sprayed (Schoop-process) metal contacts them as in film capacitors, giving thousands of layers without tiers or TSVs.
why: Attacks fact 2 (no manufacturable 3D cell): layer count comes from winding (~1,000 turns per cm of radius) instead of per-tier process steps, on roll-to-roll web lines instead of wafer fabs.
note: Winding roll-to-roll TFT memory gives layers without tiers; addressing wordlines across turns and TFT density are key doubts.

title: Grain-coarsening refresh: local-rule cellular decoder erodes error islands
idea: Borrowing how ice and metamorphic grains coarsen (small misoriented grains are eaten by their neighbors), data in each subarray tile is laid out in a 2D local parity-check code and the refresh path runs a fixed cellular-automaton rule (Toom-like majority over neighboring checks) that flips a bit only when its surrounding checks disagree. Every refresh pass shrinks error clusters a little, so errors are removed continuously in place and never accumulate to reach a global decoder.
why: Stops error accumulation between scrubs and lets raw cell BER rise ~10-100x (weaker, cheaper cells, longer refresh) for a few gates per column in the sense-amp stripe.
note: Toom-rule local correction in refresh path; needs 2D parity layout and per-column write-back logic.

title: Persistence-forecast reads: confirm predicted lines by comparing check bits only
idea: The simplest weather forecast, 'tomorrow equals today', is hard to beat. The requester keeps a predicted value for a line (last value seen, zero, or a predictor), computes its ECC check bits plus a 16-bit hash and sends them; memory reads only the stored check bits from a narrow check-bit subarray and returns a one-bit confirm, or the full line on mismatch, so a confirmed line equals the as-written data even if its cells have since decayed.
why: For predictable lines (often 30-60%) array and I/O energy fall ~10-30x; data-cell errors in confirmed lines become irrelevant, and mismatches fall back to a normal ECC read.
note: Confirm prediction by stored check bits only; hash collision false-confirm risk.

title: Every bit everywhere: Walsh-spread storage across multilevel capacitorless cells
idea: Paradox: each bit lives everywhere and nowhere. A block of N bits is written as the N analog levels of its Walsh-Hadamard transform into multilevel FeFET or gain cells; reading applies the inverse transform and slices, so a dead, stuck or drifted cell becomes small noise spread over all N bits instead of a hard error on one.
why: With N=64 a fully failed cell perturbs each bit by ~1/8 swing, absorbed without ECC, so capacitorless cells with ~1e-3 defect density become usable (cost per bit, yield).
note: Needs ~6-bit analog precision per multilevel cell; read noise accumulates across N cells in inverse transform.

title: Elo ratings for chambers, routing critical steps to winners
idea: Borrow chess and sports Elo ratings: split each lot head-to-head across chamber pairs and update every chamber's rating from downstream e-test and bit-fail results. Dispatch the most yield-sensitive steps to top-rated chambers and move older, lower-rated chambers onto tolerant layers.
why: Tool lifetime and capex: keeps depreciated tools productive instead of replacing them, +1-3% yield and deferred purchases; Elo needs far fewer comparisons than full chamber-matching DOEs.

title: Kidney-exchange chains clear mismatched DRAM inventory across buyers
idea: Apply the kidney paired-donation algorithm (integer programming over 2-6 way swap cycles plus chains started by an altruistic donor): firms post DRAM they hold but cannot use (wrong form factor, speed bin, LPDDR vs DDR, surplus allocations) and what they need, and a clearinghouse finds swap cycles that leave every party better off without cash price discovery. A buffer distributor plays the altruistic donor that starts chains.
why: Usable supply without capex: in shortages an estimated 5-10% of channel and OEM inventory is mismatched to need; cycle clearing could put most of it to work in weeks, equivalent to a fraction of a fab's output.
note: Kidney-exchange cycle clearing for mismatched DRAM; easy software pilot, gains bounded by actual mismatched inventory.

title: Capacity call options: inventory tier-ready base wafers for price spikes
idea: Works like a call option. Memory makers build and store base wafers (periphery plus first tiers) with sealed, bond-ready pads and reserved vertical links, and sell hyperscalers contracts that trigger bonding of 4-8 more tiers in a back-end line within weeks whenever contract prices exceed a strike price.
why: The 3-5 year fab lead time is what drives the ~4x price swing. Option-backed tier capacity turns weeks of back-end work into supply elasticity and funds capacity from option premiums instead of $15B fabs.
note: Back-end tier bonding still needs pre-built tier wafers; elasticity depends on stockpiling both base and tier wafers.

title: Taq-Pfu blended sense pool: cheap latches plus shared proofreading amplifiers
idea: Long-range PCR blends fast, error-prone Taq polymerase from a hot-spring thermophile with a little proofreading Pfu from the vent hyperthermophile Pyrococcus. Each bitline gets a minimum-size low-power latch that decides without restoring; row-buffer ECC flags the few suspect columns and a shared pool of large, offset-trimmed proofreading amplifiers re-senses those bitlines while their charge is still held, before a low-swing restore.
why: Tiny per-bitline latches cut sense energy and area ~5x and allow a lower-swing array; proofreading ~1% of columns restores full-size-SA error rates for ~10x lower energy per activation.
note: Tiny latches plus pooled re-sense; latch decision may disturb bitline charge.

title: Electrometer driven-guard midpoint gives the inner access transistor zero Vds
idea: 1955 lens (electrometers kill leakage by driving the guard to the signal's own potential): split the access path into two series transistors. A tiny source follower, gated by the storage node, drives the midpoint, so in hold the inner device has Vds~0 and its subthreshold/GIDL current collapses. The follower's only load is the outer transistor's off-leakage, so standby current stays at pA.
why: Subthreshold current scales with (1-exp(-Vds/kT)). Nulling Vds to <10 mV cuts the access-leakage component 10-50x, so refresh can be 4-10x rarer for access-limited cells. The two extra devices sit in a stacked tier over the capacitor.
note: Vds-nulled hold via follower; extra devices per cell cost density.

title: 1955 Shockley JFET tiers: epitaxial junction gates, no cavity gate stack
idea: A 1955 engineer gates with junctions, not oxides: grow the 3D Si/SiGe superlattice with in-situ p+ sublayers directly above and below each n-type lateral channel, so every access device is a double-gated JFET whose gates exist the moment epitaxy ends. Vertical p+ plugs tie the sublayers into wordlines; no conformal high-k/metal gate is ever deposited inside 100-tier lateral cavities.
why: Deletes the hardest 3D-DRAM module (replacement gate-all-around in lateral cavities), ~4-6 dep/etch steps per deck, and gate-oxide traps; depletion pinch-off gives a clean off-state. Fact 2 (lateral transistor blocker).
note: Removes cavity gate-stack module; dopant diffusion over 100-tier epi budget and junction-gate leakage near storage node are risks.

title: Core-memory sense winding reborn: read through segmented plate strips
idea: Core memories sensed on a separate wire, not the drive lines; in lateral 3D DRAM split the shared capacitor plate into short vertical strips per 8-cell column, hold the bitline at fixed potential, and sense the bit as charge arriving on the ~2 fF plate strip rather than the long bitline.
why: Sensing capacitance drops 20-40x, so storage voltage and swing can fall and no bitline full-swings; ~10x lower energy per access.
note: Sensing via a small segmented plate with clamped bitline; per-strip sense routing area is the doubt.
